public_rationale: OpenAI announced an agreement with Oracle for 4.5 gigawatts of additional US data center capacity on July 22, 2025 [e1]. The announcement does not establish effective prices after discounts and credits or comparable realized operating costs before and after Oracle service [e1]. It therefore establishes neither the subsidy condition nor the predicted cost increase, and does not meet the early-resolution rule [e1].
limitations: Comparable effective Oracle and Microsoft prices remain unknown.
Capacity commitments do not measure OpenAI's realized operating costs.
The packet provides no consistent before-and-after cost comparison.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If the Oracle partnership does not work like the discounted Microsoft deal, OpenAI's operating costs will rise.
conditions: Oracle partnership does not offer Microsoft-like discounted compute

statement.excerpt: It is unclear whether this partnership with Oracle will work in the same way as the Microsoft deal. If not, OpenAI’s operating costs will only go up.

from_speaker: whether this partnership with Oracle will work in the same way as the Microsoft deal
OpenAI’s operating costs will only go up
our_interpretation: The condition concerns comparable compute discounts and credits, rather than identical contractual wording.
The ordinary reading of operating costs is OpenAI's total realized operating costs, not Oracle's revenue, contract commitments or GPU list prices.
Compare equivalent reporting periods before and after Oracle compute enters service, using the same accounting treatment.
The surrounding press estimates establish an estimate basis; no formal accounting standard is specified.
No deadline or minimum increase is stated.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that Oracle lacks comparable Microsoft compute subsidies and that OpenAI's realized operating costs subsequently increase on a consistent basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The subsidy condition is established, but a completed, comparable period of Oracle service decisively shows that the predicted increase did not occur, or that operating costs fell under the relevant arrangement.

evidence.explanation: Confirms an Oracle capacity agreement. Capacity does not establish effective compute prices, absence of subsidies or OpenAI's realized operating costs.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verified effective pricing establishing that Oracle lacks comparable Microsoft discounts or credits, followed by equivalent periods of realized operating costs. A verified increase after Oracle service begins would support the forecast. A completed comparable period decisively showing no increase or a decrease would contradict it.
